**Original source:** [https://observatorioblockchain.com/bitcoin/los-etfs-ya-poseen-casi-el-8-de-todos-los-bitcoin-en-circulacion/#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=los-etfs-ya-poseen-casi-el-8-de-todos-los-bitcoin-en-circulacion](https://observatorioblockchain.com/bitcoin/los-etfs-ya-poseen-casi-el-8-de-todos-los-bitcoin-en-circulacion/#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=los-etfs-ya-poseen-casi-el-8-de-todos-los-bitcoin-en-circulacion)

**Shared with:** [ReadToRelay browser extension](https://github.com/vcavallo/ReadToRelay)



---

Los fondos cotizados en bolsa (ETFs) de bitcoin al contado en Estados Unidos han cerrado el tercer trimestre con un balance positivo, capturando entradas netas por casi $8.000 millones, según compartió el analista de Bloomberg, Eric Balchunas. En este sentido, Balchunas destacó estas cifras como una señal de crecimiento saludable y sostenido para los ETFs de bitcoin, a la vez que criticó las perspectivas poco realistas de algunos observadores del mercado que esperan un crecimiento explosivo y sin interrupciones.

[**BITCOIN Y ORO CONVIVIRÁN EN LAS RESERVAS DE BANCOS CENTRALES EN 2030, DICE DEUTSCHE BANK**](https://observatorioblockchain.com/bitcoin/bitcoin-y-oro-conviviran-en-las-reservas-de-bancos-centrales-en-2030-dice-deutsche-bank/)

## ETFs de bitcoin: $7.800 millones en el tercer trimestre

Según los datos presentados por el analista de Bloomberg, los ETFs de bitcoin lograron capturar cerca de $7.800 millones en entradas netas trimestrales, llevando la cifra total a lo largo de 2025 a más de $21.500 millones. De igual manera, Balchunas destacó que los ETFs de bitcoin ya amasan más de $57.000 millones en entradas netas acumuladas desde su debut oficial en enero de 2024.

Para Balchunas, estas cifras son evidencia de un «sólido ascenso» para la inversión institucional en BTC, mientras que [calificó](https://x.com/EricBalchunas/status/1973009826465923191) como una «fantasía infantil» la expectativa de flujos masivos constantes por «un billón de dólares diarios», argumentando que el crecimiento real se manifiesta a través de un patrón de «dos pasos adelante, un paso atrás».

![Etfs bitcoin entradas q3](https://observatorioblockchain.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/etfs-bitcoin-q3.png)

Fuente: Eric Balchunas

Según los datos de SoSoValue, el flujo de capital entrante histórico de los ETFs de bitcoin ya supera los [$57.340 millones](https://sosovalue.com/es/assets/etf/us-btc-spot) hasta el momento de la publicación, coincidiendo con los datos compartidos por Balchunas. En este sentido, las entradas netas de los ETF de BTC son lideradas por [IBIT de BlackRock](https://sosovalue.com/es/bigChart/Etf_NASDAQ_IBIT?title=iShares%20Bitcoin%20Trust\(IBIT\)&coin=BTC&page=usBTC), que supera los $60.700 millones acumulados desde su lanzamiento, acumulando $87.600 millones en activos bajo gestión (AuM) al poseer poco más de 768.200 BTC, aproximadamente un el 3.8% del suministro.

El analista de Bloomberg [catalogó](https://x.com/EricBalchunas/status/1973036594878906801) esta cifra como «una locura», señalando que «un ETF de acciones necesitaría tener $2.2 billones en activos para tener ese mismo nivel de propiedad sobre su clase de activo subyacente».

#### Evolución de los ETFs de BTC en 2025

A lo largo de 2025, la evolución de los ETFs de bitcoin han marcado un avance progresivo generalizado a pesar de momentos de contracción. El año comenzó con una fuerte entrada neta de $5.250 millones en enero, pero fue seguido por dos meses consecutivos de salidas, con $3.560 millones en febrero y $767 millones en marzo, representando el periodo de corrección más significativo del año.

El segundo trimestre marcó el inicio de una recuperación sostenida, con entradas positivas durante cuatro meses consecutivos: $2.970 millones en abril, $5.230 millones en mayo, $4.600 millones en junio y un pico anual de $6.020 millones en julio. No obstante, esta fase de acumulación se interrumpió por una leve salida de $751 millones en agosto, según las cifras de SoSoValue.

Por su parte, en septiembre la tendencia de capital positivo regresó acumulando entradas por más de $3.100 millones, con un volumen de negociación de casi $70.000 millones y llevando los activos bajo gestión a más de $150.400 millones, cerca de los $152.000 millones de máximo histórico alcanzados en julio.

![Etfs bitcoin 2025](https://observatorioblockchain.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/etfs-bitcoin-2025.png)

Fuente: SoSoValue

Es importante destacar que el valor total negociado mensualmente se mantuvo a lo largo del año en niveles elevados, oscilando entre $57.000 y $91.000 millones de dólares, lo que demuestra una alta liquidez y un mercado activo incluso en los meses de flujos netos negativos.

En conjunto, los ETFs de Bitcoin ya acumulan cerca de [1.5 millones de BTC](https://bitcointreasuries.net/), lo que los convierte en los principales poseedores institucionales de la criptomoneda, según los datos de Bitcoin Treasuries, con una cifra equivalente al 7.8% del suministro de BTC y superando los $189.600 millones.

#### Dinero institucional como catalizador para bitcoin

Los ETFs de Bitcoin se han consolidado como el principal catalizador de la demanda institucional, transformando la estructura del mercado y el comportamiento del precio de BTC en 2025. Estos vehículos de inversión regulados ofrecen una puerta de entrada familiar y regulada para que grandes instituciones, fondos de pensiones y gestores de patrimonio obtengan exposición a bitcoin.

Durante el año este flujo de capital institucional representó un impacto directo en la dinámica de oferta y demanda de bitcoin, convirtiéndose en un factor clave tras los máximos históricos establecidos por la criptomoneda. Por ejemplo, la demanda generada por los ETFs ha llegado a superar significativamente la nueva oferta de bitcoins producida por los mineros, creando un shock de demanda que ejercer presión alcista sobre el precio e incluso «absorbiendo» la presión de venta en momentos de contracción.

*PICO-8* is a [[virtual machine]] and [[game engine]] created by Lexaloffle Games. It is a [[fantasy video game console]] that mimics the limited audio-visual capabilities of 8-bit systems from the 1980s to encourage creativity and ingenuity in producing games without being overwhelmed with the many possibilities of modern tools and machines. Such limitations also give PICO-8 games a particular look and feel.

Coding on the PICO-8 is accomplished through a [[Lua (programming language)|Lua]]-based environment, in which users can create music, sound effects, sprites, maps, and games.

Users are able to export their games as [[HTML5]] web games or upload their creations to Lexaloffle's official [[Bulletin Board System|BBS]] where other users are able to play the games in a [[web browser]], and view the source code. PICO-8 games can also be exported as executable programs, which will run on [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]], [[macOS]], or [[Linux]].

Its successor is [[Picotron]], another virtual machine dubbed as a fantasy workstation with fewer constraints.

Notable games released for the system include the original version of _[[Celeste (video game)|Celeste]]_, which was created in four days as a part of a [[game jam]].

== Capabilities
The PICO-8 program integrates a [[Lua_(programming_language)|Lua]] code editor, sprite and map creation tools, and an audio sound effect and music editor. The program can load games saved locally on a computer, in the form of text or as specially encoded [[Portable Network Graphics|PNG]] images. The interface also supports a _splore_ mode, where games uploaded to the BBS can be previewed and then played in the PICO-8 program.

PICO-8 games, as well as the program's interface itself, are limited to a 128 × 128 [[pixel]], 16-color display, and a 4-channel audio output.

As of v0.1.11, users may export Pico-8 cartridges as stand-alone executables for Windows, Linux (64 bit), Mac, and Raspberry Pi.

=== Color palette
The PICO-8 palette contains 16 colors. Colors in the palette can be replaced with a different set of colors by indexing a palette update with a color ID larger than 127. These colors are not officially recognized by the creators; however, they are embraced by the community and given unofficial names.

== Development
Joseph White, who is better known by his [[nickname]] _Zep_, started to work on a [[BBC BASIC]] styled [[BASIC]] interpreter dubbed _LEX500_. Joseph later returned to LEX500 while working on another [[game engine]] called Voxatron. During development, Joseph switched from BASIC to [[Lua (programming language)|Lua 2]] [[syntax]] as the latter is easier to use and more capable as a programming language. He added built-in tools to it such as a music tracker and a map editor, and decided to rename it _PICO-8_.

Joseph got inspiration from older systems while setting the limitations of PICO-8. The 16-color palette was inspired by the [[Commodore 64]], 4-channel trackers by the [[Amiga 500]], and overall aesthetics by other 80s hardware such as the [[Apple IIe]] and the [[Famicom]]. He coined the term [[fantasy console]] to describe systems like PICO-8 that have deliberate limitations to fit a hypothetical hardware.

_PICO-BASIC v0.0._ was initially revealed at Pico Pico Cafe on May 9, 2014 by Lexaloffle Games. PICO-8 was released in 2015. However, the copyright year uses "2014", as in "2014-15" or "2014-2015".

In 2024, after 10 years of the development of the virtual machine and game engine, the Alpha release of [[Picotron]] was launched on March 14, 2024. This followed the launch of the PICO-8 software version 0.2.6 on February 28, 2024.

== Hardware
As a fantasy console, PICO-8 doesn't have an official hardware that it is based on and all of its limitations are purely emulated. [[Homebuilt computer|Homebrew computer]] and hardware hobbyists in general have made attempts to fit PICO-8 in low-end devices. PICO-8 has an official image for [[Raspberry Pi]] and [[CHIP (computer)|CHIP]] (shipped pre-installed in Pocket CHIP), and the PICO-8 community managed to directly run the official software or the games via PICO-8 emulators available in [[RetroArch]] on other [[Single-board computer|single board computers]].

While it is not possible to run PICO-8 itself on devices that are not at least [[IA-32|i386]]/[[X86-64|amd64]] or [[ARM-64]] due to several [[Library (computing)|libraries]], people have managed to emulate PICO-8 games on various low-cost [[Handheld game console|handheld consoles]] via open source emulators such as _Fake-08_ and _tac08_. The emulators function even on devices based on 32-bit [[Microcontroller|microcontrollers]] (most notably [[ESP32]]). In 2025, Infinity, a PICO-8 emulator, was released on the Google Play Store, followed in February 2026 by PicPic on the App Store.

== Adoption
The release of PICO-8 attracted the attention of programmers and video game developers who enjoyed the challenge of developing under retro-style limitations, and spurred the development of similar game engines with intentionally similar limitations. These engines are now commonly dubbed "fantasy consoles", based on the definition of the term on PICO-8's website, and roughly simulate the strict limitations of old game consoles and computers. Among these are the [[TIC-80]], which styles itself as a "fantasy computer", and the Pixel Vision 8, which allows the user to specify the simulated hardware limitations they wish to develop under. The development of fantasy consoles, as well as the development of games for them, has evolved into its own, almost exclusively hobbyist, sub-community of game development and programming.

PICO-8 gained additional attention in 2018 with the release of _[[Celeste (video game)|Celeste]]_. Originally created as a PICO-8 game for a [[game jam]], _Celeste Classic_ became one of the most popular games on the PICO-8 BBS, prompting the developers to expand the concept into a more expansive, fully realized game. The original PICO-8 version of _Celeste_ is fully playable as an [[Easter Egg (media)|easter egg]] in the full version of the game.

A [[low poly]] [[CAD]] software named picoCAD is based on PICO-8 and can be used to make models for use both inside and outside of PICO-8. It is able to export models as [[Wavefront_.obj_file|OBJ/MTL]] and also can export rotating model animations as [[GIF]]. Since its release, picoCAD has been used in many 3D PICO-8 games for the creation of models. The software got popularized in the general pixel art and retro game development community due to its unique retro aesthetic. In March of 2026, picoCAD 2 was released as a sequel to picoCAD, featuring new tools, notably for animation.

Several [[Video game remake|remakes]] and [[demakes]] of well-known retro and modern games alike are made on PICO-8. Most notable ones include _Terra_ (_[[Terraria]]_), _Poom_ (_[[Doom (1993 video game)|Doom]]_), _Fuz_ _([[Fez (video game)|Fez]]_), _Low Mem Sky_ (_[[No Man's Sky]]_), and _unDUNE II_ (_[[Dune II]]_).

PICO-8 has also seen interest among the [[demoscene]], due to its harsh restrictions attracting programmers and musicians who wish to make retro-style demos for the console.

In March 2024, several PICO-8 games were added as [[Arcade cabinet|cabinets]] to Arcade Legend, a [[Virtual reality game|VR game]] where players can play retro arcade games.

== See also

* [[CHIP-8]] – a predecessor to PICO-8 and other fantasy consoles

# v1.21.0: NApplets in Notes, drss.io Listening, WebXDC, and Pico 8

Highlights:

- **Runs napplets inside their notes**, on Android 11+ and on desktop, and
  plays **webxdc apps** attached to posts in a sandbox with no network.
- **Hosts napplets and nSites on desktop** in a bundled Chromium, at parity
  with Android.
- **Plays Pico-8** posted as `.p8.png` images, full screen, with
  touch, keyboard and gamepad controls.
- **Listens with drss.io**: episodes resume where you stopped, a listen
  queue, history, chapters, clips and speed, and drss lists that stay in sync.
- Adds a **Post Layout** setting: Indented, Full Width or Borderless notes.
- **Downloads every Home content type from your follows**, and adds forum
  threads, calendar events, code snippets and git to Home.
- Offers **web of trust from a card on Home**, with the provider's relay
  adopted in one step.
- Shows **HDR video in HDR** in the fullscreen viewer, and keeps HDR when
  compressing with H.265.
- **Plays chess over Nostr** in every build: a Chess feed with your games
  and the lobbies of your lists, draw offers, abandonment claims and end
  screens, interoperable with Jester and nostr.blue.
- **Redesigns the poll composer** in New Post, and puts the drawing button in
  every composer.
- Hardens napplets, nSites and webxdc after a security review: decrypting
  needs its own grant, cookies and WebRTC stay out of every frame, and site
  cards prefetch within a budget.
- Fixes memory leaks across view models, navigation and app-wide caches, and
  uploads that failed with "Stream Closed".

## New Features

### Napplets, nSites and webxdc

- Runs a napplet in place inside its note: Run here, a bar with Open and
  Stop, and the last frame left behind when it stops. The feed never prompts:
  anything that would ask you is refused and offered as Open instead.
- Runs webxdc apps (`.xdc` attachments and kind-1063 files) from an app card
  with Start, in their own storage per account and app, with no network, no
  WebRTC and no access to your keys. Shows a progress bar while the archive
  downloads, and opens a newer archive of the same app instead of the old one.
- Plays webxdc apps inside their notes, like napplets.
- Adds NAP-OUTBOX: napplets read and publish through people's own relays,
  with bounded routing and consent per read or signed kind.
- Follows the current NIP-5D manifests and NAP contracts: single-artifact
  manifests, verified icons and kind-aware storage. Napplets published with
  the old path-aggregate manifest must be republished.
- Takes WebRTC away from napplets, and from Tor sites on Android.
- Closes the router's local-network and DNS leaks, keeps each site's cached
  files to itself per account, and keeps a napplet's game saves when the app
  is killed.
- Tells you when Android can't open an nSite.
- Adds NAP-FS: a napplet opens and saves files you pick in the system file
  dialog, on Android and desktop, so apps like PhotoHop open. An app inside
  a note never opens a picker, and repeated dismissals back off.
- Adds NAP-INC, so napplets like Relay Browser, Blobbi and Emoji Pack
  Creator launch and talk to each other, scoped to the account they run as.
- Adds NAP-UPLOAD, which uploads through your Blossom servers, and
  NAP-COMMON: profiles, follows, NIP-19 codes, and follow, react and report
  under the same prompts as publishing.
- Adds NAP-INTENT: a napplet hands a task to another, and your favorites,
  in their order, choose which app handles it.
- Names the capabilities Amethyst doesn't support on a napplet's card
  instead of hiding Open.
- Delivers any file type a napplet loads (3D models, archives) except SVG,
  HTML and XML, which would run with the napplet's grants.
- Keeps desktop favorites across restarts, and loads their manifests at
  start on desktop as on Android.
- Hardens the hosts after a security review:
  - Relay reads decrypt DMs, gift wraps and private lists only with a
    decrypt grant, and never against a peer the app chose; only events with a
    valid signature reach an app.
  - `signEvent` needs the signer capability, which only websites hold.
  - A declined prompt backs off before it can ask again, Block denies every
    capability, and each app has one storage quota across its instances.
  - Inline launches run the newest version of an app seen on the device, so
    an old signed version can't run with today's grants.
  - Cookies and WebRTC are taken from every frame an app makes, the in-app
    browser follows the page's Tor route for WebRTC, and desktop turns off
    Chromium's network prediction.
  - `window.nostr` is offered only on https, .onion and the device itself, and
    the file chooser hands pages only other apps' files and fresh captures.
  - Site cards prefetch within one shared budget, only from public https
    servers, and not when the media setting wouldn't load images.
- Deletes the unpacked webxdc apps opened longest ago once they pass 1 GB,
  and caps a Concord channel's webxdc signals at 4 MB.

### Game Cartridges

- Adds a Play button to images that are fantasy-console carts (a 160x205
  `.p8.png`), opening a full-screen player on Android and desktop.
- Reads only the first 24 bytes of a candidate image to detect a cart, through
  the Tor-aware image client, and only when images may load.
- Plays with a sliding direction pad and O/X buttons that a thumb rolls
  between, a haptic tick per press, keyboard and gamepad keys, and sound.
- Opens the game's pause menu on Back instead of closing the player, keeps
  the screen on and hides the system bars in landscape.
- Keeps game saves when the app is killed, each cart's saves its own (by the
  hash of the cart), and only the two latest games in memory.
- Stops re-encoding a PNG cart on upload, which destroyed the game in its
  pixels.

### Chess

- Moves Chess into the navigation catalog as a feed, in release builds too:
  listed under Feeds in the drawer and menus, and pinnable to the bottom bar.
- Shows one feed driven by the top-bar list: "Mine" is the games you started,
  were challenged to or moved in; any other list is a lobby of its people's
  games, and Global every open challenge.
- Plays like a chess site: tap or drag a piece, last-move and check
  highlights, and the board always from your own side.
- Adds draw offers that ride on your next move, and a Claim win when the
  opponent has been silent for three days.
- Replays only the validated main line, so a player can't rewrite earlier
  moves, and refuses illegal moves.
- Shows end screens with the result and the score by player, move notes with
  their board, and the games a user ended on their profile's Notes tab.
- Redesigns the new-game dialog and the NIP-64 game viewer.

### drss.io

- Draws drss.io records as cards: shows, episodes, folders and feed lists.
- Resumes a long-form episode from where drss.io says you stopped, and
  marks episodes you have heard. Amethyst reads drss's listening progress
  (kind 30078) but never writes it.
- Adds a Listen screen with the episodes you are part way through, then the
  unfinished ones from your river, in one player that moves on by itself.
- Adds a listening History by day with a Feeds heard chart.
- Adds -15s/+30s, chapters from the show notes, per-feed speed, and clips
  saved as NIP-84 highlights of the episode.
- Reads a drss folder or feed list as a feed, from the Home picker or "Read
  as feed" on its card.
- Adds a drss lists organizer that sets the read and write lists, and renames,
  moves, merges and deletes lists and folders, with list pictures.
- Lets a show's owner edit its settings and on-air status.
- Keeps drss's reader records, like playback progress, out of feeds.

### Post Layout

- Adds a Post Layout setting with three modes: Indented (the author picture
  in a column beside the post, as before), Full Width (the author on top, the
  post across the width) and Borderless (Full Width with images, videos,
  Markdown media and link cards running out to the screen edges).
- Heads a full-width repost with both authors' rows beside their pictures.

### Home

- Requests every content type Home can show from your follows, so music,
  podcasts, fundraisers and attestations no longer appear only after another
  screen loaded them.
- Adds forum threads, calendar events, zap goals, code snippets, stream clips,
  git repositories, issues and pull requests, publications and torrent
  comments to Home, with new toggles in Settings › Home.
- Loads bursty catalog kinds (ebooks, magazines, music, podcasts, git repos)
  on their own subscription so one album upload can't crowd notes out.
- Keeps git repository announcements off Home.

### Web of Trust

- Shows a circle card on Home to accounts that follow 10 or more people and
  have no trust provider, and turns web of trust on from there.
- Sends your profile, follows, mutes and relay list to the provider before
  sign-up, so the first scores start from your current graph.
- Adopts the provider's relay into your trusted, search, indexer and favorite
  relays, and moves feeds set to Global onto it.
- Redesigns the card with animated rings, a typical circle size and an
  Activate button; the provider stays a visible choice, and after Activate the
  card explains that the first scores take about 10 minutes, then closes.

### Polls

- Redesigns the New Post poll composer on the group poll's design: options
  drawn as the rows a voter taps, an empty row that takes the next option,
  Enter and Tab to move between rows, and duplicates flagged.
- Takes @ mentions, :emoji: and image links in poll options.
- Gathers the settings in one card: Vote with zaps, Multiple answers, the
  zap range and Close after.

### Publications and Payments

- Renders PressStr ebooks (kind 33953), magazines (34609) and magazine
  issues (39731) as cards, opening PDFs in the in-app reader.
- Translates and crops kind-30041 publication sections like notes, with
  Copy Translated.
- Shows a one-line "Lightning Invoice · 50 sats" or "LNURL" label where
  previews are off, instead of a wall of bech32.
- Says when an invoice expires.

### Media

- Shows HLG and PQ video in HDR in the fullscreen viewer.
- Compresses video with LightCompressor-enhanced 2.3.0: HDR video stays
  10-bit HDR with H.265 where the encoder can keep it, and is tone mapped to
  proper SDR everywhere else. iPhone Dolby Vision recordings compress instead
  of failing.
- Tells you under the H.265 switch whether a picked HDR video stays HDR or is
  converted to SDR, and why.
- Names the picked video's own resolution on the Android quality slider.
- Stops the video encode when you cancel a post.
- Adds the drawing button to every composer: comments, public messages,
  articles, listings, group DMs, edits and git issues.

## Improvements and Bug fixes

- Stops uploading to NIP-95, which is deprecated. NIP-95 files still display.
- Fixes uploads that failed with "Stream Closed" when OkHttp retried a
  Blossom or NIP-96 upload over a dropped connection.
- Encrypts each file of a multi-file NIP-17 DM under its own key and nonce,
  instead of crashing on the second file.
- Retries only the files that failed, reports errors uploaders return
  silently, and leaves files removed mid-upload out of the result.
- Stops downloading translation models for blocked languages (Hebrew,
  Indonesian and Norwegian slipped through), deletes the models of blocked
  languages, and translates Filipino notes.
- Adds a Translation Models setting: Always, Wi-Fi only or Never.
- Fixes memory leaks: view models scoped to their item, eager collectors
  added per recomposition, app-wide watchers pinning notes, chess polling
  after leaving chess, and caches that only grew.
- Bounds each Concord channel's message buffer and prunes Concord channels
  under memory pressure.
- Keeps other people's local relays (localhost, LAN, tailnet) out of the
  dialer while keeping your own, and exempts only your own from Tor.
- Stops signer rejections from crashing the app, and handles a refusal in
  each flow instead of dropping it.
- Doesn't crash when a gift wrap or seal opens to something that isn't an
  event.
- Serializes a NIP-46 signer's reloads of the paired apps' relays.
- Dedupes Blossom servers so the media servers list can't crash.
- Shows zaps to the host of service-signed live streams in the chat.
- Closes the media viewer into the thumbnail of the media on screen.
- Keeps the emoji panel open while searching.
- Seeds the profile-zap notification card from the decrypt cache.
- Centers the hidden-note warning inside reposts.
- Deletes an addressable's current version even after a cleanup.
- Keeps a saved account saved across a transient login of it.
- Clears a screen's view models when navigation hands it new arguments.
- Switches tabs from the drawer's Navigate rows when the drawer stands in for
  the bottom bar.
- Paints the theme background under navigation, so going back on a light
  window no longer flashes dark.
- Makes Namecoin resolution errors selectable, and replaces the dead ElectrumX
  default server.
- Offers member removal in Marmot groups to admins only.
- Fixes a crash when replacing one mention with another while editing a

#Amethyst v1.21.0: NApplets in Notes, drss.io Listening, WebXDC, and Pico 8

Highlights:

- **Runs napplets inside their notes**, on Android 11+ and on desktop, and
  plays **webxdc apps** attached to posts in a sandbox with no network.
- **Hosts napplets and nSites on desktop** in a bundled Chromium, at parity
  with Android.
- **Plays Pico-8** posted as `.p8.png` images, full screen, with
  touch, keyboard and gamepad controls.
- **Listens with drss.io**: episodes resume where you stopped, a listen
  queue, history, chapters, clips and speed, and drss lists that stay in sync.
- Adds a **Post Layout** setting: Indented, Full Width or Borderless notes.
- **Downloads every Home content type from your follows**, and adds forum
  threads, calendar events, code snippets and git to Home.
- Offers **web of trust from a card on Home**, with the provider's relay
  adopted in one step.
- Shows **HDR video in HDR** in the fullscreen viewer, and keeps HDR when
  compressing with H.265.
- **Plays chess over Nostr** in every build: a Chess feed with your games
  and the lobbies of your lists, draw offers, abandonment claims and end
  screens, interoperable with Jester and nostr.blue.
- **Redesigns the poll composer** in New Post, and puts the drawing button in
  every composer.
- Hardens napplets, nSites and webxdc after a security review: decrypting
  needs its own grant, cookies and WebRTC stay out of every frame, and site
  cards prefetch within a budget.
- Fixes memory leaks across view models, navigation and app-wide caches, and
  uploads that failed with "Stream Closed".

## New Features

### Napplets, nSites and webxdc

- Runs a napplet in place inside its note: Run here, a bar with Open and
  Stop, and the last frame left behind when it stops. The feed never prompts:
  anything that would ask you is refused and offered as Open instead.
- Runs webxdc apps (`.xdc` attachments and kind-1063 files) from an app card
  with Start, in their own storage per account and app, with no network, no
  WebRTC and no access to your keys. Shows a progress bar while the archive
  downloads, and opens a newer archive of the same app instead of the old one.
- Plays webxdc apps inside their notes, like napplets.
- Adds NAP-OUTBOX: napplets read and publish through people's own relays,
  with bounded routing and consent per read or signed kind.
- Follows the current NIP-5D manifests and NAP contracts: single-artifact
  manifests, verified icons and kind-aware storage. Napplets published with
  the old path-aggregate manifest must be republished.
- Takes WebRTC away from napplets, and from Tor sites on Android.
- Closes the router's local-network and DNS leaks, keeps each site's cached
  files to itself per account, and keeps a napplet's game saves when the app
  is killed.
- Tells you when Android can't open an nSite.
- Adds NAP-FS: a napplet opens and saves files you pick in the system file
  dialog, on Android and desktop, so apps like PhotoHop open. An app inside
  a note never opens a picker, and repeated dismissals back off.
- Adds NAP-INC, so napplets like Relay Browser, Blobbi and Emoji Pack
  Creator launch and talk to each other, scoped to the account they run as.
- Adds NAP-UPLOAD, which uploads through your Blossom servers, and
  NAP-COMMON: profiles, follows, NIP-19 codes, and follow, react and report
  under the same prompts as publishing.
- Adds NAP-INTENT: a napplet hands a task to another, and your favorites,
  in their order, choose which app handles it.
- Names the capabilities Amethyst doesn't support on a napplet's card
  instead of hiding Open.
- Delivers any file type a napplet loads (3D models, archives) except SVG,
  HTML and XML, which would run with the napplet's grants.
- Keeps desktop favorites across restarts, and loads their manifests at
  start on desktop as on Android.
- Hardens the hosts after a security review:
  - Relay reads decrypt DMs, gift wraps and private lists only with a
    decrypt grant, and never against a peer the app chose; only events with a
    valid signature reach an app.
  - `signEvent` needs the signer capability, which only websites hold.
  - A declined prompt backs off before it can ask again, Block denies every
    capability, and each app has one storage quota across its instances.
  - Inline launches run the newest version of an app seen on the device, so
    an old signed version can't run with today's grants.
  - Cookies and WebRTC are taken from every frame an app makes, the in-app
    browser follows the page's Tor route for WebRTC, and desktop turns off
    Chromium's network prediction.
  - `window.nostr` is offered only on https, .onion and the device itself, and
    the file chooser hands pages only other apps' files and fresh captures.
  - Site cards prefetch within one shared budget, only from public https
    servers, and not when the media setting wouldn't load images.
- Deletes the unpacked webxdc apps opened longest ago once they pass 1 GB,
  and caps a Concord channel's webxdc signals at 4 MB.

### Game Cartridges

- Adds a Play button to images that are fantasy-console carts (a 160x205
  `.p8.png`), opening a full-screen player on Android and desktop.
- Reads only the first 24 bytes of a candidate image to detect a cart, through
  the Tor-aware image client, and only when images may load.
- Plays with a sliding direction pad and O/X buttons that a thumb rolls
  between, a haptic tick per press, keyboard and gamepad keys, and sound.
- Opens the game's pause menu on Back instead of closing the player, keeps
  the screen on and hides the system bars in landscape.
- Keeps game saves when the app is killed, each cart's saves its own (by the
  hash of the cart), and only the two latest games in memory.
- Stops re-encoding a PNG cart on upload, which destroyed the game in its
  pixels.

### Chess

- Moves Chess into the navigation catalog as a feed, in release builds too:
  listed under Feeds in the drawer and menus, and pinnable to the bottom bar.
- Shows one feed driven by the top-bar list: "Mine" is the games you started,
  were challenged to or moved in; any other list is a lobby of its people's
  games, and Global every open challenge.
- Plays like a chess site: tap or drag a piece, last-move and check
  highlights, and the board always from your own side.
- Adds draw offers that ride on your next move, and a Claim win when the
  opponent has been silent for three days.
- Replays only the validated main line, so a player can't rewrite earlier
  moves, and refuses illegal moves.
- Shows end screens with the result and the score by player, move notes with
  their board, and the games a user ended on their profile's Notes tab.
- Redesigns the new-game dialog and the NIP-64 game viewer.

### drss.io

- Draws drss.io records as cards: shows, episodes, folders and feed lists.
- Resumes a long-form episode from where drss.io says you stopped, and
  marks episodes you have heard. Amethyst reads drss's listening progress
  (kind 30078) but never writes it.
- Adds a Listen screen with the episodes you are part way through, then the
  unfinished ones from your river, in one player that moves on by itself.
- Adds a listening History by day with a Feeds heard chart.
- Adds -15s/+30s, chapters from the show notes, per-feed speed, and clips
  saved as NIP-84 highlights of the episode.
- Reads a drss folder or feed list as a feed, from the Home picker or "Read
  as feed" on its card.
- Adds a drss lists organizer that sets the read and write lists, and renames,
  moves, merges and deletes lists and folders, with list pictures.
- Lets a show's owner edit its settings and on-air status.
- Keeps drss's reader records, like playback progress, out of feeds.

### Post Layout

- Adds a Post Layout setting with three modes: Indented (the author picture
  in a column beside the post, as before), Full Width (the author on top, the
  post across the width) and Borderless (Full Width with images, videos,
  Markdown media and link cards running out to the screen edges).
- Heads a full-width repost with both authors' rows beside their pictures.

### Home

- Requests every content type Home can show from your follows, so music,
  podcasts, fundraisers and attestations no longer appear only after another
  screen loaded them.
- Adds forum threads, calendar events, zap goals, code snippets, stream clips,
  git repositories, issues and pull requests, publications and torrent
  comments to Home, with new toggles in Settings › Home.
- Loads bursty catalog kinds (ebooks, magazines, music, podcasts, git repos)
  on their own subscription so one album upload can't crowd notes out.
- Keeps git repository announcements off Home.

### Web of Trust

- Shows a circle card on Home to accounts that follow 10 or more people and
  have no trust provider, and turns web of trust on from there.
- Sends your profile, follows, mutes and relay list to the provider before
  sign-up, so the first scores start from your current graph.
- Adopts the provider's relay into your trusted, search, indexer and favorite
  relays, and moves feeds set to Global onto it.
- Redesigns the card with animated rings, a typical circle size and an
  Activate button; the provider stays a visible choice, and after Activate the
  card explains that the first scores take about 10 minutes, then closes.

### Polls

- Redesigns the New Post poll composer on the group poll's design: options
  drawn as the rows a voter taps, an empty row that takes the next option,
  Enter and Tab to move between rows, and duplicates flagged.
- Takes @ mentions, :emoji: and image links in poll options.
- Gathers the settings in one card: Vote with zaps, Multiple answers, the
  zap range and Close after.

### Publications and Payments

- Renders PressStr ebooks (kind 33953), magazines (34609) and magazine
  issues (39731) as cards, opening PDFs in the in-app reader.
- Translates and crops kind-30041 publication sections like notes, with
  Copy Translated.
- Shows a one-line "Lightning Invoice · 50 sats" or "LNURL" label where
  previews are off, instead of a wall of bech32.
- Says when an invoice expires.

### Media

- Shows HLG and PQ video in HDR in the fullscreen viewer.
- Compresses video with LightCompressor-enhanced 2.3.0: HDR video stays
  10-bit HDR with H.265 where the encoder can keep it, and is tone mapped to
  proper SDR everywhere else. iPhone Dolby Vision recordings compress instead
  of failing.
- Tells you under the H.265 switch whether a picked HDR video stays HDR or is
  converted to SDR, and why.
- Names the picked video's own resolution on the Android quality slider.
- Stops the video encode when you cancel a post.
- Adds the drawing button to every composer: comments, public messages,
  articles, listings, group DMs, edits and git issues.

## Improvements and Bug fixes

- Stops uploading to NIP-95, which is deprecated. NIP-95 files still display.
- Fixes uploads that failed with "Stream Closed" when OkHttp retried a
  Blossom or NIP-96 upload over a dropped connection.
- Encrypts each file of a multi-file NIP-17 DM under its own key and nonce,
  instead of crashing on the second file.
- Retries only the files that failed, reports errors uploaders return
  silently, and leaves files removed mid-upload out of the result.
- Stops downloading translation models for blocked languages (Hebrew,
  Indonesian and Norwegian slipped through), deletes the models of blocked
  languages, and translates Filipino notes.
- Adds a Translation Models setting: Always, Wi-Fi only or Never.
- Fixes memory leaks: view models scoped to their item, eager collectors
  added per recomposition, app-wide watchers pinning notes, chess polling
  after leaving chess, and caches that only grew.
- Bounds each Concord channel's message buffer and prunes Concord channels
  under memory pressure.
- Keeps other people's local relays (localhost, LAN, tailnet) out of the
  dialer while keeping your own, and exempts only your own from Tor.
- Stops signer rejections from crashing the app, and handles a refusal in
  each flow instead of dropping it.
- Doesn't crash when a gift wrap or seal opens to something that isn't an
  event.
- Serializes a NIP-46 signer's reloads of the paired apps' relays.
- Dedupes Blossom servers so the media servers list can't crash.
- Shows zaps to the host of service-signed live streams in the chat.
- Closes the media viewer into the thumbnail of the media on screen.
- Keeps the emoji panel open while searching.
- Seeds the profile-zap notification card from the decrypt cache.
- Centers the hidden-note warning inside reposts.
- Deletes an addressable's current version even after a cleanup.
- Keeps a saved account saved across a transient login of it.
- Clears a screen's view models when navigation hands it new arguments.
- Switches tabs from the drawer's Navigate rows when the drawer stands in for

- Paints the theme background under navigation, so going back on a light

- Makes Namecoin resolution errors selectable, and replaces the dead ElectrumX
